string-array.name: status_asides
string-array.item: 100.64.0.0/10 — a whole country, and you are the only one living in it.
Every packet you send takes a shortcut you will never see.
The daemon has been awake this whole time. It does not mind.
Somewhere a DERP relay just took your traffic personally.
NAT traversal: two machines behind routers, both convinced the other one goes first.
No, it is not a VPN. It is the same argument you had last week.
A tailnet is a group chat where the members are computers and nobody types.
MagicDNS is not magic. Nobody has been brave enough to say so out loud.
Your phone is a node. It has been one for a while now. Congratulations.
This card has been pressed. Nothing else happened, which is the point of it.
Held down long enough to read this, which means the connection is not the thing keeping you here.
Somewhere between here and the exit node there are eleven hops, four of them belonging to companies you have never heard of, and every one of them is having a worse day than you.
The tunnel does not care whether you are watching. It carries whatever you hand it, in order, without comment, until the battery runs out or you press this card again.
Committed at 3:14 in the morning. Tests? You are the tests.
The developer is installing the release over the working app again. The service has made its peace with this.
Somewhere in the Downloads folder are eleven APKs of the same build. Every one of them will come in handy.
"Make it work" — three words that turned into a release and a half.
The app is not at fault. The Tailscale window on the other machine is simply closed. Verified at three in the morning.
The hedgehog is still in the fog. The horse is where it was. The bundle of jam is untouched.
You pressed and held. The daemon is holding too.
Nothing is ever pushed without the magic word. It is the one law observed around here.
Half of this code was written by one neural network and half by another. Occasionally they agree.
Every easter egg is a line in strings.xml that nobody bothered to review.
More patch releases than users. Both numbers are going up.
Battery at 89 percent, three in the morning, and you are still testing account switching.
Nodes in Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Helsinki and Moscow. You are on the sofa.
A DERP relay in Helsinki has no idea who you are. Just as well.
The packet left. The packet came back. The packet will tell you nothing.
The daemon tells the coordination server it is Linux. The server believes it. Everyone is happy.
Routing below netd is like rearranging the furniture in somebody else\'s flat while they sleep.
Stare at this card long enough and it starts staring back. It already has.
This space could carry an advertisement, except there is no advertisement, no manager, no monetisation plan and, frankly, no plan.
There are more checks for "what if the daemon died" in this app than in some marriages.
New build installed, service dead, tap to start. Every release begins with a small funeral.

Between you and this line: Compose, two coroutines, a local socket, a daemon written in Go, a patch held together by good intentions, and a person who decided at three in the morning that a long press had to do something.
The native engine has been ready since 4.2.0 and is still labelled experimental. So is everything else here.
The profile bio reads "Coder -_-". Exhaustive.
Employer: "Not a Company". The pay matches.
Sixty public repositories. Count the finished ones yourself.
The most starred repository is a config editor for xray. Not this one.
Somewhere there is a "working" implementation of tailscaled under termux. The quotes are the author\'s own.
An AmneziaWG client, a Tailscale client, another proxy on top. The internet is still the same internet.
Between an OCR library for Google Lens and a manga translator, there was still time for a VPN client.
In the Downloads folder, the manga directory sits next to the tailscaled logs. Priorities are in order.
Still learning Kotlin and Go, says the profile. The code agrees on both counts.
The Homebrew tap has zero stars. Somebody had to.
Somebody reimplemented the Windows 11 Snipping Tool OCR engine in Python. For no reason. That somebody wrote this app too.
Every issue starts with "which version". Now the report answers before the question.
The diagnostics carry no node names and no addresses. The jokes carry no guarantees.
Somewhere a bug report is being typed with no version, no device and no logs. Not from here, though.
Held again. The counter went up again. This is the whole feature.
The exit node picker now marks the fastest node. The slowest one is doing its best.
A tailnet of one device is still a tailnet. It is just a lonely one.
If the service died after an update, that was not the update. That was the manufacturer.
Battery optimisation is on, the service is dead, and the issue says "app closes itself".
The About screen draws a hedgehog in fog. Nobody asked for it. Nobody regrets it.
Four counters, zero of them leaving the phone. The most honest telemetry in the business.
Between the tap and the packet there are eleven of our own checks, and the packet still makes it first.
Read this far? The line is over. The tunnel is not.
